extracted.intended_audience: students and citizens studying the North Carolina Constitution; civics/history learners
extracted.subtask_description: A question-and-answer study guide reviewing provisions, duties, limits, and procedures in the North Carolina Constitution (articles on education, homestead, punishments, militia, amendments, miscellaneous provisions). Intended to help learners understand what each constitutional section requires or prohibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: County school funding from penalties and fines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceeds of estrays, penalties, forfeitures, fines collected in counties, and payments as equivalent for exemption from military duty belong to the several counties and shall be faithfully appropriated for establishing and maintaining free public schools in the several counties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount collected in each county must be annually reported to the Superintendent of Public Instruction. Funds are county resources dedicated to free public education.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assembly power over University trustees
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly may provide for the election of Trustees of the University of North Carolina, in whom shall be vested privileges, rights, franchises and endowments granted to the Trustees, and may make provisions, laws and regulations for maintenance and management of the University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly-created provisions may be altered over time as necessary and expedient for the University's maintenance and management.

rubrics_metrics.name: University tuition benefits and appropriation of escheats
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall provide that the benefits of the University, as far as practicable, be extended to the youth of the State free of expense for tuition; property accrued to the State from escheats, unclaimed dividends, or distributive shares of estates of deceased persons shall be appropriated to the use of the University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to funds/properties accruing to the State and directs their dedication toward making university tuition free where practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of State Board of Education
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor, Lieutenant-Governor, Secretary of State, Treasurer, Auditor, Superintendent of Public Instruction and Attorney-General shall constitute a State Board of Education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governor is President of the Board and the Superintendent of Public Instruction is Secretary; Board succeeds to powers of Literary Fund and may legislate concerning free public schools and the educational fund, subject to alteration by the General Assembly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Education meeting, quorum, and expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The first session of the Board of Education shall be held at the capitol within fifteen days after organization of State government; a majority constitutes a quorum; contingent expenses of the Board are to be provided by the General Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time of future meetings determined by the Board; all Board acts, rules and regulations may be altered/amended/repealed by the General Assembly and then cannot be re-enacted by the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: University-connected departments to be established
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as practicable after adoption of the Constitution, the General Assembly shall establish and maintain, in connection with the University, Departments of Agriculture, Mechanics, Mining, and Normal Instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose is to expand practical and professional instruction in connection with the State University.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compulsory public-school attendance
rubrics_metrics.description: Every child of sufficient mental and physical ability shall attend public schools between ages six and eighteen for a term not less than sixteen months, unless educated by other means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies as a legislative power to require attendance; exemption allowed if educated by other means (e.g., private education/home instruction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal property exemption (homestead-related)
rubrics_metrics.description: The personal property of any resident to the value of five hundred dollars, to be selected by such resident, is exempted from sale under execution or other final process for collection of debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner selects the property up to the specified value; exemption protects small personal estates from forced sale for debts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homestead exemption for dwelling and city lots
rubrics_metrics.description: Every homestead and the dwellings and buildings used therewith not exceeding in value one thousand dollars (or, in lieu, any lot in a city/town/village with dwellings up to $1,000) shall be exempt from sale under execution for debt, but not from sale for taxes or obligations contracted for purchase of said premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner may select the homestead; exemption does not protect against tax sale or mortgage/purchase-related obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homestead protection for minor children after owner's death
rubrics_metrics.description: The homestead, after the death of the owner, shall be exempt from payment of any debt during the minority of his children or any one of them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a temporary shield for the homestead to support minor heirs until they reach majority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laborer's and mechanic's liens preserved
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections on personal and homestead exemptions shall not be construed to prevent a laborer's lien for work done for the person claiming such exemption, or a mechanic's lien for work done on the premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liens for labor and mechanic work have priority/are preserved despite homestead/personal-property exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Widow's homestead rights when no children
rubrics_metrics.description: If the owner of a homestead dies leaving a widow but no children, the homestead shall be exempt from the debts of her husband, and the rents and profits shall inure to her benefit during her widowhood unless she is owner of a homestead in her own right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects surviving spouse's occupancy and income from the homestead against deceased husband's debts, subject to ownership exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate estate of married woman
rubrics_metrics.description: Real and personal property of any female acquired before marriage and all property to which she becomes entitled after marriage shall remain her sole and separate estate not liable for her husband's debts, and may be devised, bequeathed, and, with written consent of her husband, conveyed as if unmarried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secures women's property rights before and after marriage, allowing independent disposition with spousal consent for conveyance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life insurance benefit for wife and children
rubrics_metrics.description: The husband may insure his own life for the sole use and benefit of his wife and children; on his death the amount insured shall be paid to wife and children or guardian for their use, free from claims of husband's representatives or creditors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures life insurance proceeds designated for family are protected from the husband's estate creditors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of homestead deeds requiring wife's assent
rubrics_metrics.description: No deed made by the owner of a homestead shall be valid without the voluntary signature and assent of his wife, signified on her private examination according to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects wife's interest in homestead by requiring her private and voluntary assent to any deed disposing of homestead property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized punishments under State law
rubrics_metrics.description: The following punishments only shall be known to the laws of the State: death, imprisonment with or without hard labor, fines, removal from office, and disqualification to hold office of honor, trust or profit under the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provision clarifies permissible punishments and frames legislative sentencing authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convict labor and restrictions on 'farming out' convicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Imprisonment with hard labor authorizes employment of convict labor on public works or other labor for public benefit, and the farming out thereof as may be provided by law; but no convict sentenced for murder, manslaughter, rape, attempt to commit rape, or arson shall be farmed out; convicts so farmed out shall be under supervision and control of the Penitentiary Board or an officer of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Farming out permitted with supervisory safeguards; specific serious offenses prohibit farming out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose-limited capital punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The object of punishments is to satisfy justice and reform the offender; murder, arson, burglary, and rape, and these only, may be punishable with death if the General Assembly so enact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Death penalty limited by statute to enumerated crimes and requires legislative enactment to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision for prisons, houses of correction and refuge
rubrics_metrics.description: General Assembly shall provide for erection and conduct of a State's Prison or Penitentiary, may provide Houses of Correction for vagrants and misdemeanants, and may establish Houses of Refuge for other classes of offenders when public interest requires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislature responsible for creating institutions tailored to restraint, correction, instruction, and employment of offenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for penal institutions and segregation of sexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislation must require that structure and superintendence of penal institutions, county jails, and city police prisons secure the health and comfort of prisoners, and that male and female prisoners never be confined in the same rooms or cell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates humane conditions and sexual segregation in confinement facilities by competent legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Public Charities and annual reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall appoint and define duties of a Board of Public Charities to supervise all charitable and penal State institutions, which shall annually report to the Governor upon their condition with suggestions for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates oversight body with reporting duties to improve administration of charitable and penal institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orphan houses and vocational training for orphans
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures for establishment of one or more Orphan Houses shall be devised for the care, education and instruction of destitute orphans, including teaching some business or trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State duty to provide institutional care and vocational preparation for destitute orphans when public interest requires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and care for idiots, inebriates, and indigent disabled
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislature shall devise means for the education of idiots and inebriates; may provide that the indigent deaf mutes, blind and insane of the State shall be cared for at the charge of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms State responsibility for institutional care and education of the mentally disabled and indigent disabled populations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-supporting principle for penal and charitable institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Legislature and Board of Public Charities should keep in view that all penal and charitable institutions should be made as nearly self-supporting as is consistent with their purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages economic measures to offset institutional costs while preserving their founding purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Militia service liability and exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: All able-bodied male citizens of North Carolina between ages 21 and 40 who are citizens of the United States shall be liable to duty in the militia; persons averse to bearing arms from religious scruples shall be exempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General Assembly to provide for organization, arming, equipping and discipline of militia and for paying when called into active service; Governor is Commander-in-Chief with power to call out militia to execute law, suppress riots or insurrections, and repel invasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Assembly and Governor powers over militia
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall provide for militia organization, arming, equipping, discipline and payment; the Governor is Commander-in-Chief and may call out the militia to execute the law, suppress riots/insurrections, and repel invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislature may enact exemptions as necessary and other laws expedient for government of the militia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional amendment procedures and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: No Convention of the people shall be called by the General Assembly unless by concurrence of two-thirds of all members of each House and unless the proposition 'Convention' or 'No Convention' has first been submitted to qualified voters at the next general election; amendments require agreement by three-fifths of each House and must be submitted at the next general election, adoption by majority making them part of the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies supermajority legislative thresholds and direct voter submission at general elections for constitutional change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retroactive punishments and continuation of indictments
rubrics_metrics.description: Indictments found for crimes committed before this Constitution take effect may be proceeded upon in proper courts, but no punishment shall be inflicted which is forbidden by this Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects against punishments newly forbidden by the Constitution even for prior offenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification for office for duel participation
rubrics_metrics.description: No person who hereafter fights a duel, assists as a second, or sends/accepts/knowingly carries a challenge, or agrees to go out of the State to fight a duel, shall hold any office in this State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes eligibility restrictions for public office based on participation in dueling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriations, accounting, and publication of public finances
rubrics_metrics.description: No money shall be drawn from the treasury but in consequence of appropriations made by law; an accurate account of receipts and expenditures of the public money shall be annually published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures legislative control of public spending and public financial transparency via annual publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics' and laborers' liens protection by legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: The General Assembly shall provide, by proper legislation, for giving to mechanics and laborers an adequate lien on the subject matter of their labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislature charged with creating statutory protections to secure payment for labor and materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenure and successor provisions for State officers
rubrics_metrics.description: In absence of contrary provision, all officers of the State shall hold positions only until other appointments are made by the Governor, or if elective, until their successors are chosen and duly qualified according to the Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies interim tenure when appointments or qualifications are pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seat of government and incompatibility of offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The seat of government shall remain at the City of Raleigh; no person who holds any office under the United States, this State, or another State or government shall hold or exercise any other office under the authority of this State or be eligible to a seat in either House of the General Assembly, with certain enumerated exceptions (militia officers, Justices of the Peace, Commissioners of Public Charities, special commissioners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines residency of government and restricts dual office-holding to avoid conflicts of interest, with limited exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of interracial marriages (historic provision)
rubrics_metrics.description: All marriages between a white person and a negro, or between a white person and a person of negro descent to the third generation inclusive, are hereby forever prohibited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute ban stated in the text; reflects constitutional prohibition of such marriages at the time of this document (historic legal content).
